facts.raw_span: A white woman in her early 40s presented with generalized pruritus of 10-years' duration
She had no other medical history
She had been treated with topical corticosteroids with no control of the symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, some of them crusted, and some excoriations located over the trunk and upper extremities
some scales and fissures were seen on her lower lip, sparing the surrounding skin, as well as inner mouth and upper lip
Blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement, along with urine porphyrin analysis were normal

The biopsy results showed spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center with cells that were CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative
Phototest with a solar simulator was carried out with the immediate reading negative for UV-B, UV-A, and visible light
erythema appeared in the area irradiated with UV-A 48 hours afterwards

She had no other medical history
She had been treated with topical corticosteroids with no control of the symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, some of them crusted, and some excoriations located over the trunk and upper extremities
some scales and fissures were seen on her lower lip, sparing the surrounding skin, as well as inner mouth and upper lip
Blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement, along with urine porphyrin analysis were normal

The biopsy results showed spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center with cells that were CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of generalized pruritus, erythematous papules, and scales and fissures on the lower lip, along with the phototest results showing delayed erythema to UV-A, are consistent with Chronic Actinic Dermatitis.
The patient's skin biopsy results showing spongiosis, erosions, and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells are suggestive of Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma.
The patient's long-standing history of generalized pruritus and the presence of erythematous papules and excoriations are consistent with Atopic Dermatitis.
The patient's phototest results showing delayed erythema to UV-A are consistent with Photodermatitis.
The patient's skin lesions, including erythematous papules and scales and fissures on the lower lip, are consistent with Lichen Planus.

rationales.F01: Generalized pruritus is a non-specific symptom
rationales.F03: Lack of response to topical corticosteroids may suggest a more complex condition
rationales.F04: Erythematous papules and excoriations are common in several dermatological conditions
rationales.F05: Scales and fissures on the lower lip may be seen in lichen planus
rationales.F07: Biopsy results showing a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and CD20 positive cells are highly suggestive of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rationales.F09: Delayed erythema after UV-A exposure is a characteristic feature of chronic actinic dermatitis and photodermatitis

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including erythematous papules and excoriations, along with the delayed erythema response to UV-A irradiation, are most consistent with Chronic Actinic Dermatitis. The skin biopsy results, while suggestive of a lymphoproliferative disorder, do not necessarily contradict this diagnosis, and the presence of a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate could be seen in Chronic Actinic Dermatitis.
